messages:
maria: Heads-up — since ~02:10 UTC we've seen repeated IOPS spikes on several eu-west1 GPU nodes during the ephemeral-cleaner window. GPU provisioning latency jumped from ~120ms to ~4.2s and about 12 attach failures. Logs:
```
[02:11:03] nvme0n1: I/O 512 bytes scheduled... qdepth 128 -> 512
[02:11:05] scrub: starting pass on /dev/nvme0n1
[02:11:06] nvme0n1: read error, sc=0x2
```
Anyone else seeing this? Suspect scrub + batch-launch overlap.

ajay: yep — seeing same on our perf counters. iops baseline ~350k spiking to ~1.2M during the window. read latency p99 for token cache jumps from ~45ms -> ~700ms. Affected services: gpu-launcher, warmup-batcher. Region: eu-west1.

noah: Noted. This pattern mirrors what we saw in ap-south last month. There we fixed by trimming scrub concurrency and adding ionice. Right now ~600 nodes in eu-west1 are >80% disk util. Proposal: delay ephemeral-cleaner job by 15m + set lower concurrency.

linh: thumbs up. Another immediate mitigation is routing low-priority (spot/preemptible) GPU launches to the dedicated fallback pool in us-west for 30m. Cost estimate: roughly +€0.8/hr per 1000 low-prio requests — but keeps tail latency down.

infra-bot: alert: ephemeral-cleaner starting on shard eu-west1-3 @ 02:10:15

sre-oncall: We're seeing kernel level `blk_mq` retries and repeated `I/O error` from nvme devices on a subset of nodes — looks like some blocks encountering errors (wear/correctable->uncorrectable). I'll mark 8 nodes for drain and trigger replacements. Also suggest lowering `scratchpool.threshold` from 0.7 -> 0.6 for the az so we stop allocating to hot drives.

ajay: Can throttle the cleaner? Current cleaner launcher uses `xargs -P 12` across batch. Suggest change to `-P 4` + `ionice -c2 -n7`. Also switch scrub process to prefer `--read-only` passes first.

maria: I'll push a canary with `-P 4` + ionice to eu-west1-3 in ~2m and watch attach failures. If failures drop under 3 we'll roll region-wide. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/d/ephemeral/cleaner-io (internal)

linh: :thumbsup: also add a small jitter to start time per-shard so they don't align at top of hour. And add an eval that ensures scratch reclaim rate doesn't regress more than 5%.

noah: Action items summary: 1) maria deploys cleaner canary with lower concurrency; 2) sre-oncall drains 8 problematic nodes; 3) ajay patches cleaner to ionice + lower parallelism; 4) ops to calculate cost & runbook for temporary routing to dedicated fallback if this recurs. I'll draft the runbook after numbers are in.

maria: Canary deployed. Initial telemetry looks better: p99 attach down to ~320ms, IOPS peak reduced to ~540k. Leaving canary for 15m to validate.

infra-bot: incident-bot: new incident created #INC-2026-341

sre-oncall: Marked nodes for drain and kicked replacement job. Will coordinate with hw-ops for any drives reporting ECC errors.

maria: Follow-ups: schedule scrub runner later (shift + jitter), implement `ionice` and lower `-P` default, and add an automatic degradation flag to mark nvme as degraded on first sc error instead of waiting for multiple failures. Filing ticket: https://tickets.redwood.internal/RED-4821 (internal).

ajay: Will open PR for cleaner changes (ionice + -P) and link it in RED-4821.

maria: Thanks all — monitoring looks stable so far, will post final after the 15m canary window.
